You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Step-by-step diagnosis: 1. The failing test `testUnion()` asserts that the union of two XPath expressions `/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]` returns the string value "John". This implies that the union operation should combine nodes from different XPath expressions and return them in document order. 2. The current bug report indicates a problem with the union operation in the core: "Core union operation does not sort result nodes according to document order". The bug report specifically references an example XML: ```xml
avaluebvalue
``` The XPath expression `string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)` should yield "avalue" because the string-value of the first node in document order is returned. But the actual value is "bvalue". This demonstrates that the union operation currently returns nodes not sorted by document order. 3. The union operation should merge two sets of nodes obtained from different XPath expressions and produce a combined node set sorted strictly in document order (the natural order nodes appear in the source XML document). The failure means the current implementation skips sorting or has incorrect sorting logic. 4. Attempts to locate relevant code: - The CoreOperationUnion class constructor was found but it only calls super with arguments and does not show union computation logic. - The union method in TreeCompiler returns a new CoreOperationUnion object with expressions. - The logic that combines node sets and sorts them is presumably inside CoreOperationUnion but no direct method `computeNodes` or similar was visible from the search. 5. From XPath specification and the bug description, the root cause is that the union operation's code which merges node sets does not perform sorting of the merged nodes, leading to nodes in the union being in evaluation order rather than document order. 6. The resulting impact is that when the string-value function is applied on the union, the first node in the union set is not the first node in document order, leading to incorrect results. In conclusion: - The core of the problem is in the union operation implementation in the JXPath core classes. - Specifically, the merged node set from the union is not sorted by document order as mandated by the XPath specs. - The fix requires modifying the union logic to ensure the resulting nodes are sorted by document order before returning them. No other recent bug reports provide additional relevant clues; they are mostly unrelated (namespace prefix, NaN comparison, binary operators with node sets). Therefore, the diagnosis is that the union node set merging code lacks or skips the sorting step by document order. This matches the test failure and bug report symptom perfectly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
